verdict.headline: Xero requires self-serve app registration for development, but full certification and high-volume limits depend on active connections and tiered paid plans.
verdict.summary: You can register a custom OAuth app instantly in the Xero Developer Portal. Testing requires no initial fees or review under the free Starter plan (up to 5 connections). Going to production with unlimited users requires moving to paid developer tiers, and Xero App Store listing requires a security assessment and 10 active beta connections.

verdict.longestPole: Accumulating 10 active customer connections and completing the security review required for App Store certification.

phases.title: Register your Xero developer app
phases.outcome: You have a client ID, client secret, and a registered app in the Xero Developer Portal.

steps.title: Create a Xero developer account
steps.details: Log in to the **Xero Developer Portal** (developer.xero.com) using your Xero user credentials. If you do not have an account, sign up for a free account.

steps.title: Provision a new OAuth application
steps.details: Navigate to **My Apps** in the developer portal and click **New App**. Enter your application name, company URL, and privacy policy URL.
steps.agentAssist: Draft the app name, privacy policy URL, and company URL to paste into the form.

steps.title: Configure redirect URIs and scopes
steps.details: Add your absolute redirect URI (e.g., `https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add` or your custom callback URL). Note that wildcards are not permitted and absolute URIs are strictly enforced.
steps.agentAssist: Generate the required list of absolute redirect URIs and granular scopes based on Composio defaults.

phases.title: Test authentication with your own account
phases.outcome: You have generated a valid authorization code, exchanged it for an access token, and verified token lifecycle properties.

steps.title: Initiate the OAuth flow with PKCE
steps.details: Trigger the authorization request against `https://login.xero.com/identity/connect/authorize` using `response_type=code`, your `client_id`, your redirect URI, PKCE (`code_challenge` with `S256`), and the required granular scopes.
steps.agentAssist: Construct the complete authorization URL with appropriate scopes and PKCE parameters.

steps.title: Exchange the code for access and refresh tokens
steps.details: Send a POST request to `https://identity.xero.com/identity/connect/token` (or `https://identity.xero.com/connect/token`) with `grant_type=authorization_code`, the authorization code, `client_id`, `client_secret`, and `redirect_uri` to retrieve your 30-minute access token and 60-day refresh token.
steps.agentAssist: Write a script or API request structure to test the token exchange automatically.

phases.title: Prepare for review and production
phases.outcome: You have onboarded 10 active beta connections and selected a paid developer tier if scaling beyond the free Starter limit.

steps.title: Gather active beta connections
steps.details: Acquire at least 10 active customer connections (using your integration within the last 30 days) to meet Xero App Store certification prerequisites.
steps.agentAssist: Draft an onboarding tracking checklist and outreach messages for beta testers.

links.label: Grow with the Xero App Store

steps.title: Select a developer pricing tier
steps.details: If your application requires exceeding the free Starter tier limit of 5 connections, upgrade to a paid developer plan (Core, Plus, Advanced, or Enterprise) as introduced in March 2026.
steps.agentAssist: Compare connection volumes and data egress requirements against Xero's tiered pricing plans.

phases.title: Go live in Composio
phases.outcome: Your custom Xero credentials are active inside Composio and ready to manage accounting workflows.

steps.title: Create custom auth config in Composio
steps.details: Configure Composio to use your Xero Client ID and Client Secret by creating a custom auth configuration for the `xero` toolkit via the Composio API or dashboard.
steps.agentAssist: Format the API payload with your `client_id`, `client_secret`, and custom redirect URI.

steps.title: Initiate connection in Composio
steps.details: Run the Composio connection flow using the custom auth config ID to verify that users are successfully redirected through `https://login.xero.com/identity/connect/authorize` back to Composio.
steps.agentAssist: Test starting a connection link via Composio to ensure the auth flow executes without error.

blockers.title: Redirect URI mismatch error
blockers.symptom: Authentication fails with an invalid redirect_uri error from Xero.
blockers.howToProceed: Ensure the redirect URI configured in your Xero Developer Portal app settings precisely matches the redirect URI sent by your application or Composio (e.g. `https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add`). Wildcards are not allowed.

blockers.title: Inactive refresh token expiration
blockers.symptom: API calls fail with unauthorized errors after periods of inactivity.
blockers.howToProceed: Xero refresh tokens expire after 60 days of inactivity. Ensure your integration implements a robust token refresh loop and prompts users to re-authenticate if the refresh token becomes invalid.

blockers.title: Granular scope mismatch
blockers.symptom: API requests are denied due to insufficient permissions or missing granular scopes.
blockers.howToProceed: Xero transitioned to granular scopes (e.g. `accounting.invoices`, `accounting.contacts`). Make sure your authorization request explicitly requests the precise granular scopes required for your API operations rather than legacy broad scopes.

nuances.title: Token Lifespans
nuances.detail: Xero access tokens expire quickly after 30 minutes. Refresh tokens remain valid for 60 days of inactivity.

nuances.title: PKCE Requirement
nuances.detail: Xero supports and encourages PKCE (S256) for secure OAuth 2.0 authorization code exchanges.

nuances.title: AI Data Training Ban
nuances.detail: Data obtained from Xero's APIs is strictly prohibited from being used to train AI or machine learning models.

nuances.title: Tiered Pricing Limits
nuances.detail: Xero enforces a tiered developer pricing model effective March 2026, restricting connection limits based on your plan (Starter free tier is capped at 5 connections).

steps: Navigate to your Composio developer dashboard and locate the Xero toolkit settings.
Create a custom OAuth configuration for Xero using your Xero Developer Portal Client ID and Client Secret.
Set the redirect URI in your Xero app settings to match Composio's expected callback URL (`https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add` or your custom callback).
Select or verify the default scopes required for your integration (including `offline_access`, `openid`, `profile`, `email`, and granular accounting scopes).
Trigger a connection test via Composio to execute the authorization flow and store user credentials securely.
